title: Natural termwise residue comparison for strictly perfect localized complexes
statement: Let S be a scheme, U an open, x in U, and choose the derived module category of the localized site. For every strictly perfect complex P [def-pc-perfect-complex], there are simultaneous isomorphisms t(P): H^0(F(P)) -> localizedResidueHomology(Q(P)) [def-sc-localized-residue-homology], where F is overEquiv followed by the module stalk at x [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] and extension along the residue quotient [def-weil-residue-field]. For every chain map alpha:P->Q of strictly perfect complexes, H^0(F(alpha)) followed by t(Q) equals t(P) followed by localizedResidueHomology(Q(alpha)). No geometric global representative or invertibility assumption is made.

proof.text: Each localized finite free term has a projective open stalk. Restriction of scalars along the open immersion stalk-ring isomorphism is an equivalence and reflects projectivity. Apply the stalk functors to the finite free retractions of P. Every transported stalk term is projective and hence flat; its upper bound is inherited from the finite support of P.
Bounded-above flat stalk complexes are K-flat. The stalk criterion then gives K-flatness of overEquiv(P). Consequently the chosen derived residue-pullback counit is invertible at this complex.

Whisker the natural counit with the homotopy quotient and use the quotient/localization comparisons to obtain a natural transformation on cochain complexes. Precompose it with the exact over-site localization comparison. Its components on strictly perfect complexes are invertible by the preceding step.

Exact global sections on the residue scheme commute with homology. The natural global-sections tensor-stalk isomorphism identifies termwise residue pullback with the residue extension of the localized stalk. Compose these natural identifications to obtain a natural transformation from localized derived residue homology to H^0(F(-)), invertible on strictly perfect complexes.
Take the inverse of each invertible component. Naturality of the original transformation, multiplied by the inverse components, gives the displayed equation for every chain map.

proof_origin.note: Source-based assembly of the chosen derived counit, exact localization and stalk tensor comparisons.

theorem exists_localizedStrictPerfectResidueHomology_iso (S : Scheme.{u}) (U : S.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (x : U.toScheme) :
    letI : (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).functor.Additive :=
      Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products _
    letI : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (IsLocalRing.residue
        (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x))).Additive :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (IsLocalRing.residue
        (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x))).left_adjoint_additive
    letI : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace x).PreservesZeroMorphisms :=
      RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor_preservesZeroMorphisms U.toScheme.toRingedSpace x
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).functor ⋙
        RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace x ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (IsLocalRing.residue
          (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x))).PreservesZeroMorphisms :=
      { map_zero := by
          intro M N
          simp only [Functor.comp_map]
          rw [Functor.map_zero, Functor.map_zero, Functor.map_zero] }
    let F := ((Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).functor ⋙
      RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace x ⋙
      ModuleCat.extendScalars (IsLocalRing.residue (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x)))
    ∃ t : ∀ (P : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
        (_hP : Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect S U P),
          ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P).homology 0 ≅
            (localizedResidueHomology S U x).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P),
      ∀ (P Q : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
        (hP : Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect S U P) (hQ : Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect S U Q)
        (α : P ⟶ Q),
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
            ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) 0 ≫ (t Q hQ).hom =
          (t P hP).hom ≫ (localizedResidueHomology S U x).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map α)
